newsitem.title: USA: PaineWebber says banking has 2 attractions.
newsitem.headline: PaineWebber says banking has 2 attractions.

text.p: PaineWebber Group's chairman said Tuesday the banking industry offered only two attractive areas for his brokerage firm, both of which would help the company compete for individual investors.
Donald Marron, who also serves as chief executive, said the firm would like to be in the trust business, as preserving estates was an important concern for individuals.

The PaineWebber chairman, who served as a panelist at a Crain's New York Business breakfast, added that the ability to offer insured deposits was the other traditional banking business he would like to enter.
"Offering people insurance on their deposits is a very important competitive advantage," he said, in answer to a question about how changing banking regulations might affect brokerages.
For brokerages to enter these two areas, Congress would have to repeal laws that go back to the Depression, which separate the banking and brokerage industries.
